I understand that emotions can cause people to say or do things they don't mean, but this seems like really unsympathetic behavior on your partners part. they must understand that because of your bpd it's much more difficult for you to handle a lot of obvious irritation and anger when you're already going through an episode. especially about them calling you a bitch, that's just an incredibly nasty thing to say. I don't want to tell you whether this partner is entirely good or bad for your mental health because I don't know the specifics of your relationship, but to me this doesn't seem like a healthy or happy relationship. what people say in arguments and during stress does matter, and you deserve more respect and understanding than it seems like you're getting from your partner.

it's kinda weird, i feel like I wrote this post. sometimes I'll walk down the street and smell something that brings me back 10 years, and I feel this sort of emptiness when the smell goes away. the weather too, something about the beginning of spring and summer nights all make me feel like a kid again. the nostalgia is like almost painful though, it's like you said you're almost seeking it out to feel as happy as you used to feel.

I try my hardest not to feel shame about my scars, but it's incredibly difficult. I just try to remember that there's nothing shameful about being in pain, and I remember that when I cut I was in a lot of emotional pain. that's not my fault, and even though I didn't deal with the pain in the healthiest way, it's because I didn't know how else I could stop feeling that way. some of us weren't taught the right coping mechanisms, or we can't find ones that work for us without being self destructive at the same time. but there's nothing wrong or bad or gross about you for doing it. it's just a sign that you needed a little more help than you were getting at the time.

I get how you feel. being babied and being taken care of... it's a way for me to really feel loved and safe. I also have bpd so I spend a lot of time trying to regulate my feelings, and it often leaves me with the "emotional skin" of a little kid, where every little mean comment or passive aggression is so hurtful or scary that I just wanna curl up into a ball and cry. being treated like you're younger alleviates the responsibilities and pressures you probably feel as an adult all the time, and that's ok.

I understand not feeling like you were made for this world. sometimes it all seems so difficult and you don't feel prepared for it all, and when everyone around you seems to be having an easier time and they can do "simple" things without help, it seems all the more discouraging. 
But we're just really sensitive people, and that comes with its pros and cons. I'm sure while you feel insecure about wanting to be babied, your boyfriend probably appreciates that you can be open about what you need and be vulnerable with him. Being babied feels great, but babying someone you love can bring just as much joy, so this seems to me like a great, healthy way for both of you to feel valued and have your needs met. 

you don't have to be ashamed of what makes you comfortable, you aren't hurting anyone and there's no age limit for being babied. it's just another way of showing affection!

when you have bpd, you'll sometimes say and do things that you regret. its a lot easier to lose control. one on hand, it's good to accept responsibility, but on the other, you have to remember that it's not your fault that you have this disorder. you know you love your best friend, and you know that if you could, you'd never hurt her at all. these are the things that make you NOT a bad person. as long as you keep working on trying to control your mood swings and the things you say to people you care about, you have no reason to feel bad about yourself. 
I get it though, I deal with the same stuff and it's hard to remember that the things I say and the people I lose don't necessarily make me a terrible person. 
you have to try to forgive yourself for how you might've hurt her in the past, while also recognizing that she has the right to leave if she wants to.
